public.title: Add a cartTotal function
public.prompt: cartTotal(cart) is added next. How will it add up the prices?
options: A for loop that pushes each price into a new array
reduce, with the sum starting at 0

hints.text: Look at addItem: this file prefers array methods to loops.
An empty cart must total 0, not throw an error.

explanations.workedExample: Write cartTotal(cart), which adds up the price of every item in the cart. Notice how reduce starts from 0 so an empty cart totals 0.
explanations.practice: Write cartCount(cart) that returns how many items are in the cart, using reduce.

secret.narration: The cart needs a total. Reduce walks the items and keeps a running sum. It starts at zero, so an empty cart totals zero instead of throwing. That is why reduce with an initial value of zero is the right choice here.

public.title: Support a discount
public.prompt: cartTotal gets a second, optional parameter for a discount. Type that parameter exactly as it will appear in the signature.

lines: +  const subtotal = cart.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0);

hints.text: Old callers pass only the cart, so the parameter must be optional.
Give it a default value that means no discount at all.

explanations.workedExample: Give cartTotal an optional discount between 0 and 1. Watch how the subtotal is computed first, then scaled by (1 - discount).
explanations.practice: Add an optional taxRate parameter that defaults to no tax.

secret.narration: Old callers pass only the cart, so the discount must be optional. A default of zero means no discount. The subtotal is computed first, then scaled by one minus the discount.

public.title: Test the total and the discount
public.prompt: The test adds a check for a 50% discount on items priced 10 and 5. What value will it assert?

hints.text: Work out the plain total first.

explanations.workedExample: Add console.assert checks for a plain total and for a 50% discount, so the behaviour from the last two steps is pinned down.
explanations.practice: Add an assertion for a 20% discount on the same items.

secret.narration: The plain total is fifteen. A fifty percent discount multiplies it by one minus point five, which gives seven and a half. The test pins down both behaviours.
